about: Structured tabletop exercises for the continuity plan (doc 88). Each exercise is a story told in injects: what happens, the question it puts to you, and the answer the plan expects. An inject with a 'check' is also tested against this machine, so the exercise cannot pass on good intentions alone. Built from the shape of NIST SP 800-84 (tabletop exercises), NIST SP 800-61 (incident phases) and the CISA ransomware guide; paraphrased, not copied.

exercises.title: Ransomware encrypts the laptop at night
exercises.story: Tuesday, 02:00. A file you opened on Friday carried ransomware. It waited, then encrypted your files and left a note. You find out at 07:00.

injects.event: The nightly backup finds the vault unreadable and the canary file encrypted.
injects.ask: Would this reach your phone before you open the laptop?
injects.expect: Yes: an alert on your phone (ntfy or a chat webhook) says RANSOMWARE SUSPECTED.

injects.event: That backup is written, but named -SUSPECT.
injects.ask: Are your clean backups still there, a week and a month back, not just the last 7 nights?
injects.expect: Yes: retention keeps one a week for 4 weeks and one a month for 3 months, and a suspect run deletes nothing.
injects.fix: ./securax backup  (nightly, by the daily-backup routine: ./securax routines)

injects.event: You see the ransom note.
injects.ask: Do you know the first three moves: unplug the network, ./securax down, and pause other nodes and the tunnel?
injects.expect: Network off first, then ./securax down. The online tunnel is outbound-only and stops with the estate. Then, on each other node, stop syncing with the laptop.

injects.event: Your other nodes sync with the laptop every 30 seconds.
injects.ask: Will sync carry the damage to the VPS and the phone?
injects.expect: The ransomware encrypts files on disk; sync carries only what the Life OS writes through its own service, so encrypted files are not synced. A thief with a sync token could still write bad data: remove the laptop from every node.
injects.fix: ./securax nodes  (on each other node: it lists the addresses it syncs with; then  ./securax nodes remove  with the laptop's address)

injects.event: The laptop is wiped and rebuilt. You need the key to open the backups.
injects.ask: Is the backup key somewhere the ransomware could not reach (your password manager, a USB stick)?
injects.expect: Yes: ./securax protect made you save it outside the laptop.

injects.event: The local backup folder is encrypted too.
injects.ask: Is there a copy off this machine, and one that was never connected?
injects.expect: An off-site copy (OneDrive keeps 30 days of versions for Microsoft 365 plans) and a monthly offline copy on a USB stick.
injects.fix: ./securax backup offsite  and, monthly,  ./securax backup offline

injects.event: You restore.
injects.ask: Has a restore from your newest clean backup been PROVEN in the last quarter?
injects.expect: Yes: ./securax continuity drill data-lost opened it as working data in a scratch twin and timed it.
injects.fix: ./securax continuity drill data-lost   then later   ./securax restore latest

injects.event: The estate is back.
injects.ask: Do you change every key in .env, the sync tokens and the Cloudflare token, since the ransomware may have read them?
injects.expect: Yes: the jewels list names each key; change each at its provider.

injects.event: Some files on the laptop belonged to other people (work, clients, family).
injects.ask: Do you know whose incident process and which regulator clocks now apply to you?
injects.expect: Their process first. Where you are the one who must report, the clocks start at detection (CERT-In counts hours).

injects.event: It is over.
injects.ask: Will you write a blameless postmortem with a mechanism that stops it again?
injects.expect: Yes, with an owner and a date for each action.

exercises.title: A key leaks and someone signs in who should not
exercises.story: An AI provider e-mails: your key was used from another country. The same evening an unknown device shows up in your Tailscale list.

injects.event: The provider reports unusual use of your key.
injects.ask: Is your spend capped, so a stolen key cannot run up a big bill?
injects.expect: Yes: the gateway's allowance caps tokens per day and month, and every provider key has its own limit at the provider.
injects.fix: set AI_BUDGET_DAY_TOKENS and AI_BUDGET_MONTH_TOKENS in local/compose/.env, and a limit in each provider's console

injects.event: You revoke the key at the provider.
injects.ask: Do you know every place that key lives (.env, backups, other nodes)?
injects.expect: The jewels list names each key and where it is; backups are encrypted, so an old copy is not a leak.

injects.event: The unknown device is on your private network.
injects.ask: Can you remove it and see who may sign in to your online addresses?
injects.expect: Remove it in the Tailscale admin page; ./securax online status lists who may sign in, and online remove takes someone off.

injects.event: You are not sure what else it touched.
injects.ask: Can you go back to a version of the code that is known to be good?
injects.expect: Yes: ./securax rollback --list shows versions that ran healthy, pinned so they cannot be lost.

injects.event: You check the estate's own records.
injects.ask: Does the gateway's audit trail show who called what, and is it tamper-evident?
injects.expect: Yes: ./securax audit verify checks the hash chain; any edited, deleted or reordered event is named.

injects.event: It is over.
injects.ask: Will you write a postmortem and turn on sign-in for the gateway if it was off?
injects.expect: Yes: AUTH_MODE=required as soon as anyone but you can reach it (./securax gateway-auth enable).

exercises.title: The VPS provider deletes your server
exercises.story: Your VPS provider suspends the account by mistake and deletes the server. The laptop is at home, switched off.

injects.event: Your phone cannot reach hub.<your domain>.
injects.ask: Is another machine ready to answer at the same address?
injects.expect: A second node runs the tunnel too (./securax online invite / join), so Cloudflare sends you there.
injects.fix: ./securax online invite  (run the line it prints on a second machine)

injects.event: You open the Life OS on the laptop.
injects.ask: Does the laptop hold the same Life OS data as the VPS did?
injects.expect: Yes: nodes sync with each other, so every node holds everyone's data.

injects.event: You need to rebuild the server elsewhere.
injects.ask: Can you rebuild it from one line and your newest clean backup?
injects.expect: Yes: install.sh --server on a new VPS, then ./securax restore latest from the off-site copy.

injects.event: GitHub is slow today too.
injects.ask: Can you get the code without GitHub?
injects.expect: Yes: a git bundle in the backup folder and a private mirror on a second host.
